quotes.text: Around 600 BC, the kingdom of Lydia minted the first true coins from electrum, a natural gold-silver alloy, each stamped with a lion to guarantee its weight.
quotes.author: Kingdom of Lydia

quotes.text: King Croesus of Lydia, whose name still means 'rich', created the first bimetallic currency system around 550 BC: pure gold and pure silver coins with a fixed exchange rate.
quotes.author: King Croesus

quotes.text: The Roman denarius was about 95 percent silver under Augustus. By 270 AD emperors had debased it to under 5 percent — and prices across the empire exploded.
quotes.author: Roman Empire

quotes.text: The word 'salary' comes from the Latin salarium — the allowance connected to salt, a substance so valuable Roman soldiers' pay was named after it.
quotes.author: Ancient Rome

quotes.text: The Byzantine gold solidus kept nearly the same weight and purity for around 700 years — historians call it the dollar of the Middle Ages.
quotes.author: Byzantine Empire

quotes.text: In 1024, Song dynasty China issued the jiaozi — the world's first government paper money, born because iron coins were too heavy for merchants to carry.
quotes.author: Song Dynasty China

quotes.text: When Marco Polo reached China around 1275, he was stunned to find money made of mulberry bark paper — and that refusing it was punishable by death.
quotes.author: Kublai Khan's China

quotes.text: Medieval England ran its tax system on split wooden tally sticks for 700 years. In 1834, burning the obsolete sticks set the Palace of Westminster on fire.
quotes.author: Medieval England

quotes.text: Cowrie shells served as money across Africa and Asia for over 3,000 years — some West African regions still accepted them as currency into the early 1900s.
quotes.author: West Africa

quotes.text: On the island of Yap, money is giant stone wheels up to 4 meters wide. One famous stone sank to the ocean floor — and everyone agreed it still counted as wealth.
quotes.author: Island of Yap

quotes.text: The Knights Templar ran medieval Europe's first travel banking: deposit money in London, carry a coded letter, withdraw in Jerusalem — 700 years before wire transfers.
quotes.author: Knights Templar

quotes.text: The Medici bank, founded in 1397, became Europe's most powerful bank using bills of exchange — a clever workaround for the Church's ban on charging interest.
quotes.author: Medici Bank of Florence

quotes.text: Sweden's Stockholms Banco printed Europe's first banknotes in 1661. Within seven years it printed too many, collapsed, and its founder was sentenced to death — later commuted.
quotes.author: Stockholms Banco

quotes.text: At the peak of Dutch tulip mania in 1637, contracts for single rare bulbs traded for more than ten times a skilled craftsman's annual income. Then the market simply stopped.
quotes.author: Dutch Republic, 1637

quotes.text: Isaac Newton, as Master of the Royal Mint, put milled edges on coins to defeat clippers who shaved silver off the rims — the ridges are still on your coins today.
quotes.author: Isaac Newton, Royal Mint

quotes.text: In 1720 Isaac Newton reportedly lost about 20,000 pounds in the South Sea Bubble — a fortune. The genius who mapped the heavens couldn't map a market mania.
quotes.author: South Sea Bubble, 1720

quotes.text: In 1720 France, John Law's paper-money experiment made him briefly the richest man in Europe — and its collapse made France distrust paper money for 80 years.
quotes.author: John Law's Mississippi Company

quotes.text: Silver from one Bolivian mountain, Potosí, flooded the world after 1545. The Spanish 'piece of eight' it produced became the first truly global currency.
quotes.author: Spanish Empire

quotes.text: The dollar sign likely evolved from the abbreviation for the Spanish peso — 'ps' written in a hurry, the s eventually crossing the p.
quotes.author: Spanish Peso

quotes.text: The word 'dollar' comes from Joachimsthaler — a 16th-century silver coin from a Bohemian valley called Joachimsthal. 'Thaler' became 'dollar' over 300 years.
quotes.author: Bohemia, 1519

quotes.text: Bad money drives out good: Tudor financier Thomas Gresham observed that when debased and pure coins circulate together, people hoard the pure ones. It's still called Gresham's Law.
quotes.author: Thomas Gresham

quotes.text: During America's Free Banking era, 1837 to 1863, over 8,000 different banks issued their own private banknotes — merchants used catalogs to spot the worthless ones.
quotes.author: United States, 1837-1863

quotes.text: The Continental — America's revolutionary war currency — collapsed so completely that 'not worth a Continental' became slang for worthless for a century.
quotes.author: American Revolution

quotes.text: The US printed its first federal paper money, the greenback, in 1862 — not backed by gold, but by the promise the Union would win the Civil War.
quotes.author: United States, 1862

quotes.text: In colonial New England, wampum — beads made from clam shells — was legal tender. Harvard once accepted tuition payments in it.
quotes.author: Colonial New England

quotes.text: Blocks of salt called amole served as money in Ethiopia for centuries — still circulating as currency in some regions into the 20th century.
quotes.author: Ethiopia

quotes.text: In November 1923, one US dollar cost 4.2 trillion German marks. Workers were paid twice a day and spent the money within minutes, before prices doubled again.
quotes.author: Weimar Germany, 1923

quotes.text: In 1923 Germany, banknotes were cheaper than firewood — families burned bundles of marks in their stoves because buying wood cost more than burning cash.
quotes.author: Weimar Germany, 1923

quotes.text: Hungary in 1946 suffered the worst hyperinflation ever recorded: prices doubled roughly every 15 hours, and the government issued a 100 quintillion pengő note.
quotes.author: Hungary, 1946

quotes.text: Zimbabwe printed a 100 trillion dollar banknote in 2009. At the hyperinflation's peak, prices roughly doubled every day.
quotes.author: Zimbabwe, 2008

quotes.text: In 1933, Executive Order 6102 made it illegal for Americans to own most gold — citizens had to sell it to the government at $20.67 an ounce, facing 10 years in prison.
quotes.author: United States, 1933

quotes.text: In July 1944, delegates from 44 nations met at a New Hampshire hotel and pegged the world's currencies to the US dollar — and the dollar to gold at $35 an ounce.
quotes.author: Bretton Woods, 1944

quotes.text: On August 15, 1971, Richard Nixon interrupted Sunday night television to announce the dollar would no longer convert to gold. Every major currency has floated ever since.
quotes.author: Nixon Shock, 1971

quotes.text: In WWII prisoner-of-war camps, cigarettes became a full currency system — with prices, exchange rates, and even inflation when Red Cross parcels arrived.
quotes.author: WWII POW camps

quotes.text: After WWII, occupied Germany ran on cigarette money for three years — until the overnight introduction of the Deutsche Mark in 1948 restarted the economy almost instantly.
quotes.author: Postwar Germany, 1948

quotes.text: The first credit card was born in 1950 after businessman Frank McNamara forgot his wallet at a New York dinner — embarrassment created the Diners Club card.
quotes.author: Diners Club, 1950

quotes.text: The world's first ATM opened at a Barclays branch in London in 1967 — inspired, its inventor said, by chocolate vending machines.
quotes.author: Barclays Bank, 1967

quotes.text: The kipper und wipper crisis of 1621 saw German states deliberately debase each other's coins — one of history's first international currency wars.
quotes.author: Holy Roman Empire, 1621

quotes.text: The Bank of England was founded in 1694 for one purpose: lending King William III 1.2 million pounds to rebuild the navy and fight France.
quotes.author: Bank of England, 1694

quotes.text: Bitcoin's first block, mined January 3, 2009, contains a hidden newspaper headline about bank bailouts — a message frozen forever into the code.
quotes.author: Bitcoin Genesis Block

quotes.text: On May 22, 2010, a programmer paid 10,000 bitcoins for two pizzas — the first real-world bitcoin purchase. The date is still celebrated as Bitcoin Pizza Day.
quotes.author: Bitcoin Pizza Day, 2010
